analysis: The supplied units are only BASE text of docs/threat-model.yaml (lines 1-897). The PR is documentation-only: it adds a header comment (head lines 43-45), asset A-018 provider_serving_availability, trust boundary TB-012 provider_to_local_addon_hold_socket, and threat T-059 for an add-on hold socket. The patch excerpt is truncated at the TB-012 description, so the full TB-012, T-059 and A-018 text and the other head ranges (811-841, 2305-2337) were not visible. No source code changes are in the supplied evidence, so I could not verify the hold-socket implementation (ProviderLoop+AddonHold.swift), signature checks, lease handling or the machine-lock fallback. I found no concrete security regression in the visible base text or patch excerpt. Base material examined: A-008 logout and revocation, TB-002 routing gates, TB-003 SE key custody, TB-007 engine, TB-009 attestation, TB-011 App Attest authorization and the T-007 to T-010 threats. The added surface is a local, same-user AF_UNIX socket that can withdraw a provider from inference, a potential availability and local-trust issue. Both processes run as the same user, so a hostile same-user process could try to trigger holds, and the 'signature check' on the add-on would then matter. This relates to ADV-001 and TB-003, with A-018 as the affected asset. Integration should check the full TB-012 and T-059 text against the actual implementation: owner-only socket permissions, peer code-signing verification, lease expiry bounds, fail-safe behavior, and whether the coordinator trusts the provider-reported busy fields in routing. The doc itself states that coordinator handling of the busy fields is separate platform work. Because the key part of the patch is truncated, needs_deeper_review is set to true.
